**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 14:57  
[EVENT] User is looking to get a portable power bank to keep their phone charged on the go.  
[CHANGE] User recently cleaned out their old phone accessories and got rid of three old phone chargers that didn't work anymore.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking to consolidate their charging setup.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended options for portable power banks:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anker PowerCore 5000: 5,000mAh capacity, compact, affordable, built-in USB-C port, priced at $15-$20.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mophie Powerstation Mini: 4,000mAh capacity, slim, stylish, USB-C port, priced at $20-$25.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anker PowerCore 10,000: 10,000mAh capacity, charges most phones 2-3 times, compact, multiple USB ports, priced at $25-$30.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Jackery Titan 10,000mAh: compact, high capacity, multiple USB ports, including USB-C, priced at $25-$30.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anker PowerCore 20,000: 20,000mAh capacity, charges most phones 4-5 times, portable, multiple USB ports, priced at $40-$45.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mophie Powerstation XXL: 20,000mAh capacity, multiple USB ports, including USB-C, priced at $50-$55.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested features to consider when choosing a power bank: capacity, ports, size and weight, brand and quality, additional features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended looking for a power bank with a USB-C port to future-proof the charging setup.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested looking for a power bank with multiple USB ports to charge multiple devices at once.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended considering a power bank with Power Delivery (PD) charging for fast-charging USB-C phones.  
[PREFERENCE] User is leaning towards the Anker PowerCore 10,000.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Confirmed that the Anker PowerCore 10,000 is a fantastic choice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Discussed the pros and cons of a power bank with a built-in USB-C cable versus a separate cable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pros of a built-in cable: convenience, compactness, reduced clutter.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cons of a built-in cable: limited flexibility, length limitations, compatibility issues.
